Carbon nanotubes have a high purity level of 96%.
The composites were prepared with a 1% loading level of carbon nanotubes.
The reflection loss values increased with increasing particle size.
The best value was observed in composites with dimensions in the range of 48-78 nm.
The effective bandwidth was determined as 10.27 GHz.
Dielectric loss causes the composite materials to interact with electromagnetic waves and weaken them.
The mechanism of radar absorption in carbon nanotube composites is primarily attributed to improved impedance matching, interfacial scattering, and dielectric and magnetic losses.

The study introduces an innovative and efficient approach to fabricate a promising EM absorption material with characteristics such as lightweight, robust absorption capability, and a broad absorption bandwidth.
The composites were prepared using a Network Analyzer covering the frequency range from 8 to 12 GHz.
The reflection loss values were measured using a transmission/reflection method.
The composites were evaluated using X-ray Diffraction (XRD) and Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) analyses.
The magnetic properties of the composites were analyzed using a Vibrating Sample Magnetometer (VSM).
The study shows that the radar absorbing properties of carbon nanotube composites can be optimized by adjusting the particle size.
The effective bandwidth of the composites with the best particle size range was determined as 10.27 GHz.
The study has potential applications in stealth technology, aerospace, and defense.
